topic: Manipur Gets Elected Government After President's Rule

subtopics.title: Kuki-Zomi and Meitei Violence
subtopics.summary: Violence erupted between Kuki-Zomi tribals and the Meitei community, the first clash of its kind in three decades in Manipur. A key trigger was the Meitei demand for Scheduled Tribe (ST) status, which has persisted since 2012. A 2023 High Court direction to consider that request added to tensions with Kuki groups.
facts: Violence between Kuki-Zomi tribals and Meitei community
First clash of this kind in three decades in Manipur
Demand for ST status for Meitei community persisted since 2012
Meitei Tribe Union petitioned Manipur High Court for tribal status
Meiteis lost tribal status after the 1949 merger
High Court judge directed state to consider Meitei ST request in 2023
Kukis fear ST status would allow Meiteis to buy land in prohibited hill areas
State evicted 16 Kuki households over forest encroachment, sparking protests
State withdrew from suspension of operations agreement with KNA and ZRA in March 2023

subtopics.title: Historical Background and Divides
subtopics.summary: Meiteis make up 52 per cent of Manipur's population and live mainly in valley areas covering about 10 per cent of the state. Hill areas cover 89 per cent of the land but have only 20 of the 60 assembly seats, while Meiteis hold 40. Meiteis are restricted from buying land in about 90 per cent of Manipur, whereas tribals can buy land in the Imphal Valley.
facts: Meiteis comprise 52 per cent of Manipur's population
Valley areas cover just 10 per cent of the state
Hill areas cover 89 per cent of the state's land
Hill areas have 20 MLAs; Meiteis hold 40 of 60 assembly seats
Meiteis restricted from buying land in 90 per cent of Manipur
Tribals can buy land in Imphal Valley
Nagas and Kukis demand greater political autonomy or separate administrative units
Meitei concerns over inaccurate 2020 census figures and delimitation process
Concern over rapid growth of villages in Churachandpur due to migrants

subtopics.title: Key Records and Judicial Review
subtopics.summary: Manipur has had President's Rule the most number of times, 11, followed by UP, J&K and Punjab. The first three instances were in Punjab, PEPSU and Andhra. In S.R. Bommai vs Union of India (1994), the Supreme Court held that the President's power to dismiss a state government is not absolute.
facts: First three President's Rule: Punjab (1951), PEPSU (1953), Andhra (1954)
Most instances: Manipur (11), UP (10), J&K (9), Punjab (8)
Longest total duration: J&K, then Punjab, then Puducherry
Shortest total duration: Uttarakhand
Longest single period: J&K
Shortest single periods: West Bengal, Bihar, Maharashtra
38th Amendment Act of 1975 made the President's satisfaction final and not challengeable in any court
Beyond 1 year, extension needs a National Emergency in operation and Election Commission certification
S.R. Bommai vs Union of India (1994): power to dismiss a state government is not absolute
Till Parliament approves, President can only suspend the Legislative Assembly
